title: Arizona State Retirement System Has $222.48 Million Stake in Apple (AAPL)
text:
Tweet
Arizona State Retirement System lifted its stake in Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) by 2.0% in the fourth quarter, according to the company in its most recent 13F filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission. The firm owned 1,314,651 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock after acquiring an additional 25,164 shares during the period. Apple accounts for approximately 2.2% of Arizona State Retirement System’s holdings, making the stock its biggest position. Arizona State Retirement System’s holdings in Apple were worth $222,478,000 at the end of the most recent reporting period.
Several other large investors also recently modified their holdings of the company. Fagan Associates Inc. lifted its stake in shares of Apple by 1.7% in the 4th quarter. Fagan Associates Inc. now owns 70,636 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $11,954,000 after acquiring an additional 1,180 shares during the period. Pinnacle Financial Partners Inc. raised its holdings in shares of Apple by 8.6% in the 4th quarter. Pinnacle Financial Partners Inc. now owns 95,056 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $16,086,000 after purchasing an additional 7,508 shares in the last quarter. Buckley Wealth Management LLC bought a new stake in shares of Apple in the 4th quarter worth approximately $13,334,000. Evermay Wealth Management LLC raised its holdings in shares of Apple by 25.6% in the 4th quarter. Evermay Wealth Management LLC now owns 28,649 shares of the iPhone maker’s stock worth $4,848,000 after purchasing an additional 5,845 shares in the last quarter. Finally, NuWave Investment Management LLC bought a new stake in shares of Apple in the 4th quarter worth approximately $625,000. 58.14% of the stock is owned by institutional investors. Apple stock opened at $193.46 on Friday. The company has a market capitalization of $980.86 billion, a price-to-earnings ratio of 21.01, a P/E/G ratio of 1.44 and a beta of 1.29. The company has a current ratio of 1.46, a quick ratio of 1.37 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.80. Apple has a twelve month low of $142.20 and a twelve month high of $194.20. Apple (NASDAQ:AAPL) last released its quarterly earnings data on Tuesday, May 1st. The iPhone maker reported $2.73 earnings per share for the quarter, beating the Thomson Reuters’ consensus estimate of $2.69 by $0.04. The firm had revenue of $61.14 billion for the quarter, compared to analyst estimates of $60.94 billion. Apple had a net margin of 21.55% and a return on equity of 39.97%. The company’s revenue for the quarter was up 15.6% compared to the same quarter last year. During the same quarter in the prior year, the business earned $2.10 EPS. equities research analysts forecast that Apple will post 11.43 earnings per share for the current year.
The firm also recently announced a quarterly dividend, which was paid on Thursday, May 17th. Shareholders of record on Monday, May 14th were given a $0.73 dividend. This represents a $2.92 annualized dividend and a yield of 1.51%. This is an increase from Apple’s previous quarterly dividend of $0.63. The ex-dividend date was Friday, May 11th. Apple’s payout ratio is currently 31.70%.
Apple announced that its board has approved a stock buyback program on Tuesday, May 1st that allows the company to repurchase $100.00 billion in shares. This repurchase authorization allows the iPhone maker to purchase up to 11.9% of its shares through open market purchases. Shares repurchase programs are typically a sign that the company’s leadership believes its stock is undervalued.
A number of research firms recently commented on AAPL. UBS Group set a $210.00 target price on shares of Apple and gave the stock a “buy” rating in a report on Thursday. Goldman Sachs Group reiterated a “neutral” rating and issued a $164.00 target price on shares of Apple in a report on Tuesday. Royal Bank of Canada boosted their target price on shares of Apple from $203.00 to $210.00 and gave the stock an “outperform” rating in a report on Tuesday. BidaskClub upgraded shares of Apple from a “hold” rating to a “buy” rating in a report on Tuesday, May 29th. Finally, Morgan Stanley reiterated an “overweight” rating and issued a $214.00 target price (up from $200.00) on shares of Apple in a report on Thursday, May 24th. They noted that the move was a valuation call. One research analyst has rated the stock with a sell rating, sixteen have issued a hold rating, thirty-two have assigned a buy rating and two have issued a strong buy rating to the stock. The stock currently has an average rating of “Buy” and an average target price of $205.54.

Following the completion of the sale, the insider now directly owns 68,044 shares of the company’s stock, valued at $12,897,059.76.
